nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Drifting algae that bloom where river nutrients arrive. When a bloom dies and sinks, bacteria break it down and use up oxygen.

nodes.name: Smooth cordgrass
nodes.desc: Fringe marshes that shelter young shrimp, crabs and fish.

nodes.name: Zooplankton
nodes.desc: Tiny grazers of phytoplankton. Adult menhaden and bay anchovies eat them.

nodes.name: Gulf menhaden
nodes.desc: A filter feeder. Wikipedia says juveniles eat mainly phytoplankton and adults mainly zooplankton. A major forage fish for the Gulf.

nodes.name: Bay anchovy
nodes.desc: A small schooling fish that eats zooplankton. Wikipedia notes anchovies may temporarily increase in hypoxic water.

nodes.name: Eastern oyster
nodes.desc: Filters algae from the water. Wikipedia notes oysters face more disease under hypoxia.

nodes.name: Seafloor worms & clams
nodes.desc: Bottom dwellers that feed on sinking algae and detritus. They suffocate when oxygen drops very low.

nodes.name: Brown shrimp
nodes.desc: Young shrimp grow in coastal marshes and then move offshore, where trawlers first reported the dead zone in 1950.

nodes.name: Atlantic croaker
nodes.desc: Hunts worms, small crustaceans and other bottom prey.

nodes.name: Spotted seatrout
nodes.desc: Hunts shrimp, anchovies and small fish in bays and marsh edges.

nodes.name: Red snapper
nodes.desc: A reef fish and one of the Gulf's major catches. Eats shrimp, crabs and fish.

nodes.name: Red drum
nodes.desc: Hunts crabs, shrimp and fish in marshes and bays.

nodes.name: Blue crab
nodes.desc: An omnivore that eats oysters, worms and carrion.

nodes.name: Sea nettle
nodes.desc: A jellyfish. Wikipedia says jellyfish can survive hypoxia and may increase when competitors and predators leave.

nodes.name: Kemp's ridley turtle
nodes.desc: A small sea turtle that feeds mainly on crabs.

nodes.name: American white pelican
nodes.desc: A winter visitor to Gulf bays and estuaries. Nests on lakes in the interior and also follows the Mississippi River in winter.

nodes.name: Bottlenose dolphin
nodes.desc: Eats fish, shrimp and squid, often herding schools toward shore. Large sharks including bull sharks prey on it.

nodes.name: Bull shark
nodes.desc: A coastal shark that enters estuaries and river mouths and eats fish and dolphins.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Warm, bright surface water lets blooms grow fast in summer.

nodes.name: River nutrients
nodes.desc: Nitrogen and phosphorus carried by the Mississippi, mostly from farm runoff and sewage, fuel the summer blooms.

nodes.name: Bottom-water oxygen
nodes.desc: Warm, layered water traps oxygen-poor water near the bottom. Bottom dwellers that cannot leave suffocate when oxygen falls very low.

nodes.name: Bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead algae. In summer this uses up bottom-water oxygen and creates the dead zone.
